questions.question: Give the IUPAC names of: (a) CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH (b) CH₃CHO (c) HOCH₂CH₂OH (d) CH₃CH(CH₃)COOH.
questions.solution:
**(a) CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH.** The longest chain with the carboxyl carbon has 4 carbons; the acid suffix is '-oic acid'.

**Butanoic acid**

**(b) CH₃CHO.** The longest chain has 2 carbons and the aldehyde carbon is always C1; the suffix is '-al'.

**Ethanal**

**(c) HOCH₂CH₂OH.** The longest chain has 2 carbons and carries two hydroxyl groups, so the parent is ethane with the ending '-diol'.

**Ethane-1,2-diol**

**(d) CH₃CH(CH₃)COOH.** The longest chain with the –COOH carbon has 3 carbons, and a methyl group is on C2.

**2-Methylpropanoic acid**

Remember the priority order of characteristic groups: carboxylic acid > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol > amine. The characteristic group is always included in the parent chain and must receive the lowest locant.
questions.knowledgeNote: Carboxylic acids use the '-oic acid' ending with the COOH carbon numbered 1; alcohols use '-ol'.
